elaine: Heads-up: Support ticket mentioned model-catalog shows different embedding dims for "aurora-lite" and "aurora-lite-quant". Customers get runtime errors in SDK when sending to a vector index expecting fixed dim. Can someone add a small compatibility note + SDK snippet that validates dims and auto-resizes (with warning)?

derek: I can handle the doc note. Plan: short table in the model card listing dims per variant, and an SDK snippet that raises a clear error or pads/truncates with a flag.

sam: For the pad/truncate snippet, prefer explicit opt-in. People shouldn't silently change semantics. Suggest name `ensure_vector_dim(vec, target_dim, mode="error")` with modes error/pad/trunc.

kai: Agreed. Also add a short migration note in the catalog: if you used external indexes created from older variants, include a reindex command and the expected compatibility delta. I have the qdrant/pinecone reindex steps.

derek: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1024 1 includes model card table, migration note, and two SDK snippets (py/js).

sam: Adding the python snippet here:
```python
def ensure_vector_dim(vec, target_dim, mode="error"):
    if len(vec) == target_dim:
        return vec
    if mode == "error":
        raise ValueError(f"vector dim {len(vec)} != {target_dim}")
    if mode == "pad":
        return vec + [0.0] * (target_dim - len(vec))
    return vec[:target_dim]
```

kai: Also included a tiny benchmark note: padding increases index size slightly; expect ~0.5% storage increase for typical 1536->1540 pad. I added a short compatibility paragraph noting expected cosine-drop ~0.01-0.03 for padding vs retraining.
